name: protocol_strings_as_python_reads_them
description: The GDScript codec reads strings as protocol.py does: strict UTF-8, no NUL, no leading byte-order mark; anything else is refused without an engine error per bad byte, and good text (accents, a mid-string U+FEFF, the most a field holds) reads back whole. The encoder refuses the same, so this side never builds a frame the server or its own decoder refuses.

steps.msg: a broken two-byte sequence is refused
a code point past U+10FFFF is refused
a sequence cut short is refused
a leading byte-order mark is refused
accents, a mid-string U+FEFF and a four-byte character read back whole

steps.assert: bom.is_empty() and codec.last_error.ends_with('starts with a byte-order mark')
steps.msg: and the encoder refuses what the decoder (and protocol.py) refuse: a leading byte-order mark (review M1 protocol 2)
while good text, a mid-string U+FEFF too, encodes and reads back
